adb_path_source.evidence: adb is not on PATH in the Bash tool on this machine; resolve via config or drive it from Python

console_encoding.evidence: the Windows console is cp1252; app labels with non-Latin text raise UnicodeEncodeError without it

pm_clear_variant.evidence: on a multi-user Samsung ROM the bare form returns Success but leaves the session intact

appbar-shares-label-with-primary-button.evidence: desc=Login matched both the back header and the submit button on the same screen
appbar-shares-label-with-primary-button.text: The app bar often carries the same accessibility label as the screen primary button, so a first-match label lookup taps the back header and navigates away. Constrain body taps below the app-bar band, and never use a button label as a screen-identity marker.

back-up-the-project-blob-before-ui-work.evidence: a 5.9MB blob with 23 notes was backed up before UI changes and made the work reversible
back-up-the-project-blob-before-ui-work.text: The project blob carries the whole board (screens, notes, layout) and is several MB. Snapshot it to disk before doing anything that opens a second dashboard tab or rewrites notes.

dashboard-hidden-tab-freezes-overlay.evidence: notes and selection state were correct on the server while the hidden tab showed none
dashboard-hidden-tab-freezes-overlay.text: requestAnimationFrame is throttled in a hidden browser tab, so the dashboard overlay (cards, notes, selection) stops repainting while the underlying data stays correct. A board that looks empty in a background tab is a rendering artefact -- verify against the server before debugging the UI.

dashboard-stale-tab-clobbers-project.evidence: a second tab autosaved an empty note set over a populated board
dashboard-stale-tab-clobbers-project.text: Two dashboard tabs open on one project is data loss: a tab that loaded before annotations restored will autosave a note-less blob over the good one, and the stale tab wins. Keep one tab per project.

dump-shows-top-window-only.evidence: an auth-error modal and a progress overlay each made a correct rejection look like the input had been accepted
dump-shows-top-window-only.text: dump_hierarchy() returns only the topmost window, so a dialog or a blocking progress overlay hides the screen underneath. A missing screen marker therefore means something is covering the screen, not that navigation happened. Never judge the result of a submit while a request is still in flight.

empty-dump-means-wait.evidence: a dump 5s after launch contained only com.android.systemui while a screenshot showed a fully rendered app
empty-dump-means-wait.text: An empty or status-bar-only UI dump right after launch means the UI has not rendered yet, not that the app is broken. Wait for text, not for node count -- a splash screen publishes nodes with no text.

hard-reload-after-editing-static-assets.evidence: a verified-correct fix appeared to do nothing until a hard reload
hard-reload-after-editing-static-assets.text: dashboard.js and dashboard.css are served with a cache-busting query and still get served from cache. After editing either, hard-reload (ctrl+shift+R) before concluding a change did not work.

reactive-validation-defeats-diffs.evidence: five validation checks reported blocked-but-silent against a screen that was showing a specific message
reactive-validation-defeats-diffs.text: Forms that validate while you type already show their error before the submit tap, so a before/after text diff around the tap finds nothing. Baseline the pristine screen on arrival and diff against that, excluding input field values.

screenshot-before-believing-a-dump.evidence: four separate dump misreads each presented as a confident defect
screenshot-before-believing-a-dump.text: Before reporting anything negative derived from a UI dump, capture a screenshot. Every false defect this harness has produced was a dump misread, not an app fault.

server-needs-a-real-restart.evidence: documented in the repo troubleshooting notes and re-confirmed in use
server-needs-a-real-restart.text: server.py runs with reload=False, and a stale process keeps holding port 8000 while the new one fails to bind -- so edits appear to have no effect. Check who owns the port before debugging the code.

system-dialogs-are-invisible-to-package-.evidence: a notification-permission prompt after a data wipe made the app dump look empty
system-dialogs-are-invisible-to-package-.text: Android permission prompts belong to com.android.permissioncontroller, so any dump filtered to the app package sees an empty screen. Scan the raw dump when a launch appears to produce nothing.
